units.Dirección quiere el número y la tendenci: Leadership wants the number and the trend. No filters, generous margins and a single lead visual. The detail goes below, and small.
units.El equipo comercial lo consulta cada día: The sales team checks it every day. Quick filters at the top, a full row of KPIs and comparisons you can read at a glance.
units.Quien analiza acepta densidad si a cambi: Analysts accept density if it gets them answers. Filters down the side, more visuals and more detail, but the hierarchy stays.
units.Un cliente externo, por ejemplo, no tien: An external client, for example, doesn't need to know our acronyms or our internal language. They need context, a few KPIs, a clear message and no unnecessary jargon.
units.Y hay otra pregunta que a veces se me ol: And there's another question I sometimes forget: where will they look at it?
units.No es lo mismo un comité mensual frente: A monthly committee in front of a big screen, where probably only the first KPIs get read, isn't the same as checking the report on a phone between two meetings.

units.Antes de leer un gráfico, ya estamos mir: Before we read a chart, we’re already looking.
units.Laboratorio perceptivo: veinte cuadrados: Perception lab: twenty squares that change colour, size, position and grouping.

units.Primero, orden: lo alineado se lee como: First, order: what’s aligned reads as a system.
units.Después, prioridad: el protagonista va d: Then, priority: the protagonist goes where reading starts.
units.En una pantalla occidental suele ser arr: On a Western screen that’s usually the top left. It’s a tendency, not a law: a strong signal can pull the eye anywhere.
units.No intento que el lector procese una can: I don’t expect the reader to process an infinite amount of information at once.
I simplify. And I set priorities.
units.La investigación habla de unos pocos “bl: Research talks about a few “chunks” at a time, with a lot of variation depending on the task. I don’t use it as a magic number: I use it as a reminder that the reader can’t take in everything.
units.Dos barras de 1,2 y 1,5 millones de euro: Two bars of 1.2 and 1.5 million euros, first misaligned, then on a common baseline with the 300 thousand euro difference drawn in.
units.El ojo encuentra patrones rápidamente. C: The eye finds patterns quickly. Comparing two specific values is another story.
units.Una base común ya reduce el trabajo: aho: A common baseline already reduces the work: now I’m comparing lengths, not loose positions.
units.Y si la diferencia es el mensaje, la dib: And if the difference is the message, I draw it. That way nobody has to work it out.
units.Muchas veces no necesito explicar qué co: Often I don’t need to explain which things are related. I just have to place them well.
units.Veinte puntos que se perciben como grupo: Twenty dots that are perceived as different groups depending on proximity, similarity, common region and connection.
Twenty dots, with no apparent relationship.
units.Lo que está cerca parece del mismo grupo: What’s close together looks like the same group.
units.Lo que se parece, también. Aquí leo colu: So does what looks alike. Here I read columns even though the spacing is the same.
units.Un fondo compartido crea un grupo más fu: A shared background creates a stronger group than distance.
units.Y una línea une más que cualquier otra c: And a line joins things more than anything else.
units.Una buena composición puede explicar una: A good composition can explain a relationship before a single word appears.
units.Una vez que sé qué quiero comunicar, emp: Once I know what I want to communicate, I start taking things away.
units.Vuelve el dashboard del principio. El mi: The dashboard from the beginning is back. The same one. This time, step by step.
units.Primero, elimino lo que decora pero no a: First, I remove whatever decorates but doesn’t help reading.
units.Después reviso lo que está compitiendo c: Then I look at what’s competing with the data.
units.La retícula se queda solo donde ayuda a: Gridlines stay only where they help read a value.
Ten colours. None of them meant anything.
units.Y si solo necesito destacar una cosa, no: And if I only need to highlight one thing, I don’t need ten colours.
units.Las etiquetas pueden vivir junto al dato: Labels can live next to the data.
units.Los decimales tampoco tienen que demostr: Decimals don’t need to prove they exist either.
units.Lo secundario puede seguir estando. Solo: Secondary things can stay. They just have to weigh less.
units.Elige un elemento de un dashboard y mira: Pick an element from a dashboard and see what question I ask it.
units.La sombra no dice nada sobre el dato. Fu: The shadow says nothing about the data. Out.
units.El logo ya está en la cabecera. Repetirl: The logo is already in the header. Repeating it six times adds nothing.
€1,572,340.00 forces you to count digits. €1.57m reads at a glance.
units.El contexto se queda, pero en gris: no p: The context stays, but in grey: it can’t beat the protagonist.

units.¿Lo quito y nada cambia?: If I remove it, does nothing change?
units.¿Solo queda más bonito?: Does it only make it prettier?

units.Cuando hay demasiado detalle, busco una: When there’s too much detail, I look for a structure before removing information.
units.Veinte subcategorías. Se puede leer, per: Twenty subcategories. It can be read, but it’s hard work.
units.Cuatro familias. La primera lectura cabe: Four families. The first read fits in a glance.
units.Y el detalle vuelve a estar disponible c: And the detail is available again when someone asks for it.
units.En Power BI: una jerarquía con drill-dow: In Power BI: a hierarchy with drill-down, or a detail page.
units.La primera lectura puede ser simple <em>: The first read can be simple without losing the second layer.
units.Quitar ruido es solo la mitad. Después t: Removing noise is only half the job. Then I have to decide what I want you to see first.
Position can tell you where to start.
units.Y una anotación puede explicar por qué m: And an annotation can explain why it’s worth looking.
I don’t use colour to decorate the report. I use it when I want to highlight a figure, set something apart or direct attention.
units.Categorías distintas, sin orden. Pocas,: Distinct categories, with no order. Few of them, with well-separated shades.
units.De menos a más. Un solo tono que gana in: From less to more. A single hue that gains intensity.
units.Dos direcciones desde un punto neutro qu: Two directions from a neutral point that means something: zero, the target.
units.El color puede ayudar muchísimo, pero no: Colour can help enormously, but it shouldn’t be the only signal.
units.Tres líneas de ventas por canal. Sin col: Three sales lines by channel. Without colour, the legend stops working; with direct labels and different strokes, the meaning holds.
units.Si quito el color, quiero que <em>la his: If I take the colour away, I want the story to keep working.
units.Intento que solo una pequeña parte del g: I try to keep the main emphasis on only a small part of the chart.
units.No porque exista un 10 % mágico.<br><b>P:
Not because there’s a magic 10%.
Because when everything stands out, emphasis stops working.
units.Diez barras. Cuando todas destacan igual: Ten bars. When they all stand out equally, none does; when only one does, the eye goes straight to it.
units.El gráfico correcto no es el más vistoso: The right chart isn’t the flashiest. It’s the one that best answers the question.

units.¿Qué quieres que vea?: What do you want them to see?
units.Los mismos puntos se transforman en líne: The same points turn into a line, bars, a ranking, a histogram, a scatter plot or a stacked bar depending on the task chosen.
units.Una tarjeta KPI tiene que responder en u: A KPI card has to answer three questions at a glance: how much, which way and compared with what.
units.Sin gráfico, el número se queda solo. Lo: With no chart, the number stands alone. I use it when space is tight, when the row has many KPIs or when the trend doesn’t change the decision.
units.La sparkline es una línea del tamaño de: A sparkline is a word-sized line: you don’t read it value by value, you read its shape. It works for continuous series and answers one question: is today’s figure a peak or the norm?
units.Las columnas funcionan cuando cada perio: Columns work when each period counts separately: sales by month, orders by week. The last one, the current period, is a shade darker.
units.Tarjeta KPI: etiqueta Ventas Q4, valor 1: KPI card: label Q4 sales, value 1.57 million euros, change of plus 24% against Q4 2024 and a grey mini chart on the right.
units.<b>Etiqueta.</b> Qué se mide y de qué pe: Label. What is measured and for which period. Small, grey and in capitals: it names, it doesn’t compete.
units.<b>Valor.</b> Lo más grande de la tarjet: Value. The biggest thing on the card. Short format with its unit: €1.57m, not €1,572,340.00.
units.<b>Delta.</b> La flecha dice hacia dónde: Delta. The arrow says which way it’s moving; the colour, whether it’s good news. Never colour alone.
units.<b>Referencia.</b> ¿Frente a qué? Año an: Reference. Compared with what? Previous year, target, 12-month average. A delta without a reference means nothing.
units.<b>Minigráfico.</b> Contexto, no protago: Mini chart. Context, not the protagonist: on the right, about two-fifths of the width, in grey and with no axes.
units.Cuatro tarjetas KPI. Ventas sube y es bu: Four KPI cards. Sales goes up and it’s good news. Gross margin falls against target and it’s bad. Turnover falls and it’s good. Cost per lead goes up and it’s bad.
units.Fíjate en la fila: dos deltas bajan y do: Look at the row: two deltas go down and two go up, and the colour doesn’t follow the sign. If it did, someone would celebrate rising staff turnover. That’s why I separate direction from judgement, and the arrow is still there when the colour can’t be seen.
units.Dos detalles más: cuando el KPI ya es un: Two more details: when the KPI is already a percentage, the change goes in points (pp), not in %. And the reference is explicit, as IBCS asks: previous year, plan or forecast, but always stated on the card.

units.Tendencia y comparación con presupuesto: Trend and comparison with budget at the top; region and product below, sorted so the ranking reads itself.
units.La cascada es el visual natural del P&L:: The waterfall is the natural visual for a P&L: it shows how you get from revenue to EBITDA. No filters, because it’s a closing report.
units.Barras para comparar áreas, una barra 10: Bars to compare departments, a 100% bar for composition and a slope chart to see who improves and who gets worse between two years.
units.El embudo tiene sentido aquí porque las: The funnel makes sense here because the stages are sequential. Traffic in an area chart; channels in bars.
units.Embudo de checkout, evolución del GMV y: Checkout funnel, GMV trend and a scatter plot for the question that always comes up: is price holding back conversion?

units.El layout es el esqueleto de la historia: Layout is the skeleton of the story.

Then I place the big idea.
units.Después, la métrica que merece verse pri: Then, the metric that deserves to be seen first.
Then, the visual that explains why.
units.Y los elementos que interactúan deben pa: And the elements that interact should look related.
units.No existe un espaciado mágico. A mí me a: There’s no magic spacing. What helps me is working with a system that keeps a steady rhythm: every distance is a multiple of 8.
units.Cada distancia se decidió a ojo: 13, 7,: Each distance was decided by eye: 13, 7, 22, 5… None of them is wrong on its own, but together they have no rhythm and the figures don’t line up.
units.8 px entre textos que van juntos, 16 px: 8 px between texts that belong together, 16 px of padding inside the card and 16 px between cards. The canvas margin, 24. In Power BI I apply it to the position, size and padding of every object.
units.Tres tarjetas KPI con sus distancias mar: Three KPI cards with their distances marked. With irregular spacing every distance is different; with the 8-point system they’re 8, 16 and 24 pixels and the figures line up.
units.El espacio vacío no está vacío. Separa,: Empty space isn’t empty. It separates, groups and adds emphasis.
units.Todo pegado: los márgenes y los huecos m: Everything crammed together: margins and gaps are all the same size, so nothing groups and nothing stands out. The eye doesn’t know where to start.
units.Con el mismo contenido, doy margen al li: With the same content, I give the canvas a margin and leave more room between groups than within them. Without a single line, two blocks read clearly: the figures and the charts. That’s proximity working for you.
units.Rodeo de aire la cifra que importa y red: I surround the figure that matters with space and scale back the rest. The space around it makes it the protagonist, with no need for colour or an exaggerated size.
units.El mismo informe con tres usos del espac: The same report with three uses of space: everything crammed together; grouped into figures and charts with more space between groups than within them; and with the main figure surrounded by space.
units.Antes de colocar nada, elijo dónde se va: Before placing anything, I choose where it’s going to be read.
units.Carta (816 × 1056) es un documento, no u: Letter (816 × 1056) is a document, not a screen. I use it when the report is printed or exported to PDF: vertical reading, more text, tables and a comment next to each chart.
units.Tooltip (320 × 240) es una página que ap: Tooltip (320 × 240) is a page that appears when you hover over a data point. It fits a KPI and a minimal visual: the detail arrives only when someone asks for it.
units.En Power BI, el móvil no es otro informe: In Power BI, mobile isn’t another report: it’s a mobile layout of the same one, where you rearrange the visuals into a single column. In the tool I simulate it with 400 × 640. Few KPIs, one per row, and one visual per screen.
units.Personalizado sirve para una pantalla co: Custom is for a specific screen or for scrolling pages: here, 1280 × 1440, two screens tall. Watch out: in the service, the default view fits the whole page to the window; for it to scroll you have to choose «Fit to width».
units.Los lienzos de Power BI dibujados a la m: Power BI canvases drawn to the same scale: 16:9, 4:3, letter, tooltip, mobile and a custom scrolling page.
units.Un dashboard se lee por capas: contexto,: A dashboard is read in layers: context, metrics, message and detail.
Zone B takes up almost twice as much as A. The eye reaches the detail before the message, and the decision is made on the wrong figure.
units.Header, KPIs, Zona A y Zona B, en ese or: Header, KPIs, Zone A and Zone B, in that order and with that weight. As a starting point: Zone A takes about half the height and B a little over a quarter.
units.Lo que no cabe no desaparece: baja a un: What doesn’t fit doesn’t disappear: it moves to a tooltip or a drill-through page, where whoever needs it can find it.
Wireframe with a header, KPIs, Zone A and Zone B. First the detail zone takes up more than the main one; then the main one wins its space back.
units.Cada zona tiene un peso. El alto se repa: Each zone has a weight. The height is shared out in proportion.
units.Primero resto lo fijo: margen, header y: First I subtract what’s fixed: margin, header and gaps. What’s left is shared between the KPIs, Zone A and Zone B according to their weight. My starting point is 2 · 5 · 3: a compact KPI row, the message with half the space and the detail with the rest.

units.El plano no cambia. Cambia el recorrido: The wireframe doesn’t change. What changes is the path I expect the eye to take.
units.Son tendencias, no leyes. Un color o un: They’re tendencies, not laws. A strong colour or size breaks any pattern; that’s why I place things first and then check where the eye comes in.
units.El mismo plano con tres recorridos de le: The same wireframe with three reading paths overlaid: a Z pattern, an F pattern and horizontal layers that lose attention from top to bottom.
units.En el <a href=\"#c03\">capítulo 03</a> v: In chapter 03 we saw how the eye groups things. Here, how to check it on a dashboard.
units.Son los cinco principios que diagnostica: These are the five principles PBI Mockup Creator diagnoses while you design. Each one, applied well and badly on the same wireframe.
units.Lo que está cerca se percibe como un gru: What’s close together is perceived as a group.
units.<b>Qué es.</b> El cerebro agrupa lo que: What it is. The brain groups what’s closest, even when there’s no other visual connection.
units.<b>En un dashboard.</b> La separación en: On a dashboard. The spacing between zones decides which blocks read as a unit. If it varies from one place to another, the reader groups the wrong things and the story breaks.
units.Entre bloques del mismo nivel, de 8 a 20: Between blocks at the same level, 8 to 20 px and always the same. If I want to separate two groups, I give them more room on purpose. Below 8, everything looks like one block; above 28, loose pieces.
What’s biggest and first is read first.
units.<b>Qué es.</b> No leemos todo con la mis: What it is. We don’t read everything with the same attention: size, position and visual weight create a reading order.
units.<b>En un dashboard.</b> Si la Zona B ocu: On a dashboard. If Zone B takes up more than A, the eye reaches the detail before the message, and the decision is made on the wrong figure.
units.Recorrido: contexto → métricas → análisi: Path: context → metrics → analysis. Zone A at least 85% of B’s height. Always a header if leadership or someone external will read it.
units.Lo que se parece, se percibe como de la: What looks alike is perceived as the same family.
units.<b>Qué es.</b> Misma forma, color, tamañ: What it is. The same shape, colour, size or texture make two elements look like part of the same group, even when they’re apart.
units.<b>En un dashboard.</b> Si KPIs y gráfic: On a dashboard. If KPIs and charts look the same, the eye can’t tell monitoring from analysis. Similarity is the dashboard’s grammar: what plays the same role looks the same.
units.Hasta 6 KPIs por fila y hasta 3 visuales: Up to 6 KPIs per row and up to 3 visuals per zone. The same corner radius on every card.
units.El ojo completa formas y necesita espaci: The eye completes shapes and needs room to breathe.
units.<b>Qué es.</b> Tendemos a completar form: What it is. We tend to complete incomplete shapes and read white space as the edge of objects. Negative space isn’t empty: it’s structure.
units.<b>En un dashboard.</b> Márgenes y separ: On a dashboard. Margins and gaps create that space. Without it, the dashboard looks cluttered even with little data. With too much, it looks unfinished.
units.Entre un 20 y un 40 % del lienzo libre,: Between 20 and 40% of the canvas left free, and at least 16 px of margin on all four sides.
units.El contenido tiene que despegarse del fo: Content has to stand out from the background effortlessly.

units.Una tabla de 150 clientes es un mar de n: A table of 150 customers is a sea of numbers. What makes it readable isn’t the table, it’s what surrounds it: a search box that filters by customer, sector, segment or country, a subtitle that says how many customers I’m looking at, and colour reserved only for variances (▲ green, ▼ red). In greyscale, everything else fades and the only thing still catching the eye is those signals.

The two boxes on the left let you change the metric and what it’s compared against, so users explore without getting lost. The delta is the only thing in colour: the comparison is what turns a number into news.

The post is about a specific problem: an extreme value can squash the scale and make everything else look flat, and a well-built visual zoom avoids it without hiding the data. It’s the same principle as the «doing it right» gallery.
